translations.title: Fourth Secret Poem to Madeleine
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Sky and the Birds Came to Rest
translations.text:
The sky and the birds came to rest
on two cypresses that the warm wind almost entwined
like a pair of lovers in their final kiss.
The house beside the Rhine was like something from a novel,

with its great windows, its pointed roof,
above which the weather vane cried at times
to the wind that gently asked, What is wrong?
An owl was nailed above the door.

We talked in the wind behind a low wall,
or read the inscription on a stone placed
there in memory of a dead man, upon which
you very often sat for a long time:

“Gottfried, apprentice of Brühl, in the year six hundred thirty,
was murdered here.
His sweetheart, in deep sorrow:
Requiem aeternam dona ei Domine.”

The setting sun covered the mountain in purple,
and our love bled like the currant bushes
that starred the pale German autumn.
Night, weeping light, died at our feet.

And so our love mingled with death.
Far away, beside a bonfire, gypsies sang.
A train passed with open eyes along the opposite bank.
We watched the riverside villages for a long time.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: If I Die Far Away
translations.text:
If I die far away on the battlefront,
you will weep one day, O Lou, my great love,
and then the memory of me will fade from the earth
like a shell exploding on the battlefront,
a lovely shell like mimosa in bloom.

Later that memory, burst open in the air,
will cover the whole earth with my blood:
the valley, the sea, and the star passing by
like the golden fruit of Baratier in spring.

Present in every forgotten and living thing,
I will kindle the color of your rosy breasts,
kindle your lips and your burning hair.
You will not grow old, and everything that exists
will take on new life under beloved fate.

The inescapable flight of my blood through the world
will give a brighter glow to the dying sun,
make the flower redder and the sea deeper.
An unheard-of love will descend upon the world,
and your lover will have greater power in your body.

If, dying far away, my memory is forgotten,
remember, Lou, in the purest ecstasies of your life,
on your days of ardor and loving passion,
that my blood is the source of that future joy;
and as the most beautiful, be the happiest,
O my love, O my only one, O my boundless madness!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Airplane
translations.text:
What have you French done with Ader of the air?
A word was his; now it is nothing.

He fitted the limbs of ascent
with a name in the French language, then lacking one,
and Ader became a poet and called them avion.

O people of Paris, and you of Marseille and Lyon;
all you rivers and mountains of France,
city dwellers and country folk,
the instrument for flight is called avion.

Sweet word that would have charmed Villon;
future poets will set it in their rhymes.

No, your wings, Ader, were not nameless
when the grammarian came to master them,
to forge a learned word with nothing airy in it,
where the heavy hiatus and the ass beside it—airplane—
make a long word, like one from Germany.

It took Ariel's murmur and voice
to name the instrument that bears us to the sky:
the sigh of the breeze, a bird in space,
and a French word passing through our mouths.

The avion! Let the avion rise through the air,
glide above mountains, cross the seas,
and vanish still farther away.

Let it trace an eternal furrow in the ether,
but let us keep its gentle name, avion,
for the five nimble letters of that magical name
had the power to open the moving heavens.

What have you French done with Ader of the air?
A word was his; now it is nothing.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Five Poems to Lou
translations.text:
Winter has come and I have seen the buds again
on the fig trees, the hedges. Love, we are moving
toward peace in this wartime spring we inhabit.
We are well. Here, listen to the cries of men.
A Japanese sailor scratches his left eye with
the big toe of his right foot.

Along the road of exile come the children of kings.
My heart circles you like a kolo in which
young Serbian soldiers dance beside a sleeping
virgin.

The blond infant hunts his lice in the rain.
A Belgian who has crossed into the Netherlands reads
a newspaper that speaks of me.
On the dike a queen looks in terror at the battlefield.

The nurse closes his eyes before the dreadful wound.
The bell ringer sees the bell tower fall like a ripe pear.
The English captain whose ship is sinking smokes his last
opium pipe.

Men cry out. I cry toward the spring of peace
that is coming.
Listen to the cries of men.
But I cry toward you, my Lou; you are my peace, my spring.
You are my dear Lou, the joy I await.
For it, our joy, I prepare for death.
For it, our joy, I keep faith with life.
For it, our joy, armies fight.
We aim at the decimated infantry by means of a mirror.
Shells pass like shooting stars.
Prisoners go by in sorrowful troops.
And my heart beats only for you, dear one,
my love, my Lou, my art and my artillery.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: In Libyan Ivory You Carve Your Dream...
translations.text:
In Libyan ivory you carve your dream
of love; you exalt the nymph of your being,
and between lips of Olympian design
your chisel enamels flowers of pearl.

You suffer; the block with its smiling gaze,
where the fever of life is absent,
lies motionless: its master's blood
does not leap beneath the icy curves.

Heaven hears your cry. “Rise again,”
Apollo calls; the elusive beauty
turns to flesh and rises into life;

you kiss her beneath the Attic ceiling,
and within the net of her living lashes
you find a blue without limit or depth...
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: She
translations.text:
Buried in the dark quarry
of my scorched brain, pure
as a diamond in coal, her face shines
as it did when I first saw it.

And, like a devoted stonecutter, my love
waits to place upon her the humble garment
in which I now clothe her ideal figure
as artist, woman, and enchantress.

If anything pulses in my Poem, a drop
of water in the desert, if it leaves a trace
or manages to bind a broken soul;

if the spark of a verse tears through the shadows
—a light floating in oblivion—
it is her distant radiance: it is She!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Sphinx
translations.text:
Everything in you disturbs me and everything deceives me,
from your mouth, where one senses passion
that turns the petals of that feline rose purple,
to the fair, restless flicker of your lashes.

Everything in you is against me; your smile wounds me
like a spell, and through your divine speech
deception walks across a field of flowers,
cold as a venomous beast.

With your martyr's face you are an act of vengeance.
Your little hands strangled my hope,
and your flower is a spurge half-hidden in tulle.

Butterfly wings feed your lamp;
let this verse, which your prose inspired, burn in it:
you are a lie with blue eyes!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: In an Album
translations.text:
There are ladies born to appear one day
crowned with a lyrical flower;
to live your dreams, gentle Chivalry,
in the arms of a young man in ruff and fleece.

They were born under the star of Gallantry
to perfume a century, like Maintenon,
or ennoble their line with a fierce race
that stains a coat of arms' gold with a hundred eagles.

There are hands that could guide with golden reins
the swan that bears chosen souls
across languid lakes to an Olympian land!

There are fingers whose touch transforms everything:
pebbles into gems, prose into poems,
and the flower of the crossroads into a heraldic lily!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: There Is a Moment
translations.text:
There is a moment at twilight
when things shine brighter,
a fleeting, pulsing moment
of lingering intensity.

The branches turn to velvet,
the towers polish their outlines,
a bird engraves its silhouette
upon a sapphire ceiling.

The afternoon falls silent, gathers itself
for the forgetting of light,
and a gentle gift enters it:
melancholy stillness,

as though the world were collecting
all its goodness and beauty,
all its faith, all its grace
against the coming shadow.

My being flowers in that hour
of mysterious flowering;
I carry a twilight in my soul,
a dreamer's calm,

where the new shoots of springtime hope
burst forth, and where I am drunk
on the scents of some garden
that lies beyond!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
